content.title: About
content.content: Pickled vegetables are a mix of various vegetables (cucumbers, carrots, cauliflower, peppers, etc.) that have been preserved in a brine made of vinegar, salt, spices, and sometimes sugar. The pickling process keeps them crunchy and gives them a characteristic tangy‑sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickling has been used since ancient times as a way to extend the shelf life of vegetables.
The acidity of the brine (usually 2–3 % acetic acid) inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria.
Traditional recipes often include spices such as mustard seeds, dill, coriander, and black pepper.
In many countries pickled vegetables are considered a national dish (e.g., Korean kimchi).
Pickled vegetables can be served cold or hot (e.g., hot pickled cucumbers).

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Vegetables retain most of their vitamin C, vitamin K, and provitamin A (beta‑carotene) content.

items.title: Source of probiotics
items.content: Fermented pickles (such as sauerkraut) contain beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Most pickled vegetables are low in calories, making them a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phytochemicals like polyphenols remain in pickled vegetables and help combat free radicals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity of the brine stimulates gastric juice production, improving digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Large amounts of salt can raise blood pressure; people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Acid reflux
items.content: The acidic brine may aggravate heartburn in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some spices (e.g., mustard seeds) can cause allergies.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage above 4 °C can allow growth of harmful bacteria such as Clostridium botulinum.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled vegetables can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, sandwiches, sushi rolls, stews, or used as a side dish for meat. Slice them thin for rolls or serve whole on appetizer platters.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in the original brine in an airtight container. Properly stored, they stay good for 2–3 weeks. Discard if the smell becomes sharp, mold appears, or the brine turns cloudy.
